title: Surjective module-sheaf maps induce degreewise surjective symmetric-algebra maps
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal E$ be quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-modules [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and let $u:\mathcal F\to\mathcal E$ be an $\mathcal O_S$-linear morphism surjective as a map of sheaves: every local section of $\mathcal E$ lifts to $\mathcal F$ on an open covering of its domain. Use the symmetric algebra sheaves with their canonical degree-one maps $j_{\mathcal F}$ and $j_{\mathcal E}$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] and their symmetric-degree grading [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]. The unique induced morphism of $\mathcal O_S$-algebra sheaves
$$\operatorname{Sym}(u):\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal F)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E),\qquad \operatorname{Sym}(u)\circ j_{\mathcal F}=j_{\mathcal E}\circ u,$$
preserves every symmetric degree, is the identity of $\mathcal O_S$ in degree zero, and is surjective as a map of sheaves in every degree $n\geq0$. Explicitly, for every open $U\subseteq S$ and $t\in\operatorname{Sym}^n(\mathcal E)(U)$ there are an open covering $U=\bigcup_k U_k$ and sections $v_k\in\operatorname{Sym}^n(\mathcal F)(U_k)$ with $\operatorname{Sym}(u)(v_k)=t|_{U_k}$.

source.place: Tag 01CJ (lemma-presentation-sym-exterior), surjectivity of each symmetric power; Section 01CF (section-symmetric-exterior), quotient construction and symmetric grading.

proof.text: Apply the canonical sheaf universal property [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra-core] to the module morphism j_E composed with u, obtaining a unique algebra-sheaf map a extending u. The equation for scalars is the commutativity condition of a morphism under O_X. Sectionwise, the canonical symmetric algebra lift of u agrees with a after the sectionMap: prove this on scalars and generators, then on sums and products.

The explicit affine grade [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra] is the nth power of the degree-one range. Prove by submodule-power induction that both module-induced symmetric algebra maps and restriction preserve this power: scalars give degree zero, addition preserves membership, and multiplying by a generator raises the degree by one. Naturality of the sectionMap then shows that the sectionMap of a degree-n element on any open is homogeneous in the affine-test sense [def-trf-symmetric-homogeneous-sections]. For a homogeneous input section, apply its affine-test witness on each affine subopen and then the module-induced symmetric algebra map. Naturality of a and the generator comparison from Step 1 prove degree preservation.

For any open U and degree-n element s of the sectionwise symmetric algebra of E, prove that s lifts near every x in U to a degree-n element of the sectionwise symmetric algebra of F, by submodule-power induction. A scalar lifts on U itself. For a sum, intersect the two lifting neighborhoods and restrict both lifts, then add. For a product of a degree-one generator and a degree-i element, local surjectivity lifts the module generator near x; intersect that neighborhood with the one supplied by induction, restrict both lifts, and multiply. Step 2 gives the required degree membership; naturality, additivity and multiplicativity give the lifting equations. Thus zero, n=0, and empty sums require no exceptional cases.

For a homogeneous section t on U and x in U, choose an affine neighborhood V of x contained in U [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Its affine-test witness [def-trf-symmetric-homogeneous-sections] gives a degree-n sectionwise element s mapping to t restricted to V. Apply Step 3 to s and x, then apply sectionMap to the resulting lift on W contained in V. By Step 2 this is homogeneous; the sectionMap naturality and Step 1 identify its image under a with t restricted to W. Choose one such W and lift for each point x of U. This point-indexed family is in Type u, lies below U, and its supremum is U since the neighborhood chosen for x contains x. If U is empty the index type is empty. These witnesses prove the requested degreewise local surjectivity.

lean.statement: theorem exists_map_degreewise_locallySurjective {X : Scheme.{u}} (F E : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] [E.IsQuasicoherent] (u : F ⟶ E) [PresheafOfModules.IsLocallySurjective (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) u.val] : ∃ a : algebra F ⟶ algebra E, (∀ (U : X.Opens) (x : F.val.obj (op U)), a.right.hom.app (op U) ((inclusion F).val.app (op U) x) = (inclusion E).val.app (op U) (u.val.app (op U) x)) ∧ (∀ b : algebra F ⟶ algebra E, (∀ (U : X.Opens) (x : F.val.obj (op U)), b.right.hom.app (op U) ((inclusion F).val.app (op U) x) = (inclusion E).val.app (op U) (u.val.app (op U) x)) → b = a) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (U : X.Opens) (s : (algebra F).right.obj.obj (op U)), IsHomogeneousSection F n U s → IsHomogeneousSection E n U (a.right.hom.app (op U) s)) ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens) (r : X.presheaf.obj (op U)), a.right.hom.app (op U) ((algebra F).hom.hom.app (op U) r) = (algebra E).hom.hom.app (op U) r) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (U : X.Opens) (t : (algebra E).right.obj.obj (op U)), IsHomogeneousSection E n U t → ∃ (I : Type u) (V : I → X.Opens) (hV : ∀ i : I, V i ≤ U), iSup V = U ∧ ∃ v : ∀ i : I, (algebra F).right.obj.obj (op (V i)), (∀ i : I, IsHomogeneousSection F n (V i) (v i)) ∧ ∀ i : I, a.right.hom.app (op (V i)) (v i) = (algebra E).right.obj.map (homOfLE (hV i)).op t)
